editorNote: A thin day for verifiable material: one primary filing tied to Alphabet's data-center build-out made it through. Disclosed facts only; nothing here is investment advice.

stories.headline: Black Hills signs agreements to power a planned Google data center in Cheyenne, with $1.8 billion of its own generation capex
stories.summary: Black Hills Corp. will provide up to 590 MW of grid-connected service and invest $1.8 billion in 2027–2029 to build 564 MW of company-owned generation. Google provided $399 million of refundable advances for equipment procurement, and the filing says Google bears all costs of serving the site.
stories.whyItMatters: The filing discloses who pays for new power capacity serving an Alphabet data center, with Black Hills projecting about $150 million of net income in 2030 from the project.
